claim: Researchers can create and edit shared scenario responses without a model while retaining exact-parent human attribution, immutable lineage, visible stale-draft recovery, and deterministic concurrent sibling convergence.
proved: The selected-scenario product surface exposes a manual Write response path that performs no model or network call.
Creating a human response stores the installation researcher ID and display-name snapshot, exact scenario/response/revision identities, timestamp, and null provider/model/run provenance.
Editing appends one immutable exact-parent human revision and retains every earlier model or human revision in lineage.
A stale edit is refused before any Yjs mutation; the product keeps the unsaved draft visible, disables Save revision, and offers Reload shared.
Two disconnected product-controller edits against the same parent survive as siblings and converge to the same deterministic current response on both peers.
Malformed response history disables manual writes, generation, and regeneration before a new event, credential lookup, model call, or network request.
The product renders no more than 50 response cards per page and no more than the 50 most recent lineage revisions per expanded card.
The product states that installation-provided researcher identity is not authenticated and that response work does not alter the policy draft.
The same response workspace receives both generated model variants and manual human edits; no parallel response store was introduced.
notProved: Two packaged physical installations edited the same response through a real Drive workspace and displayed the sibling lineage after reconnect.
Authenticated participant identity, trusted timestamps, moderation, or explicit sibling-branch reconciliation beyond deterministic projection.
Packaged pointer, keyboard, focus, screen-reader, narrow-layout, reduced-motion, and every-theme interaction.
Near-limit response counts, 500,000-character bodies, or 100,000-revision histories meet a measured latency and memory budget.
A live local or paid provider generated or regenerated a response in this evidence run.
A release/updater artifact contains this development checkpoint.
